Testimony of Rep. Holly T. Sargent introducing
LD 2098, An Act to Update Certain Higher Education Statutes
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs
Good morning, Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy and fellow members of the Joint
Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs. I am Holly Sargent, and I represent
District 147. I am pleased to call your attention to LD 2098, An Act to Update Certain Higher
Education Statutes.
This bill allows the Maine DOE to collect initial application fees for out-of-state higher
education institutions applying for degree-granting authorization or program approval in Maine.
LD 2098 amends current statute to give the Higher Education Administration Fund the authority
to receive the fees. This bill also allows the State Board of Education to forgo a duplicate
institutional review if that institution has already passed a Maine review in the last five years.
The Maine DOE will present testimony on this bill, and I respectfully request that you defer any
specific questions regarding the content to them. Thank you for your time, and I look forward to
working with you as we deliberate the bill.

Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy, and Members of the Joint Standing Committee on

My name is Michael Perry, and l am here today representing the Maine Department of
Education speaking in support of L.D. 2098, An Act to Update Certain Higher Education Statutes
This bill adds initial application fees for out-of-state higher education institutions applying for degree-granting authorization or program approval in Maine. Maine is one of a minority of states that does not collect fees of any kind from applicant institutions, which has the effect of weakening consumer protections against potentially low-quality or predatory institutions in Maine. The bill also gives the Higher Education Administration Fund the authority to receive the fees.

The processes for degree granting authorization and program approval are both spelled out in

05-071 Rule Chapter 149: Procedures for Obtaining Authorization for Institutions of Higher

,

Education to Confer Academic Degrees or to Offer Degree Courses/Programs in the State of

Maine. The process is time- and la bor-intensive and relies primarily on work capacity from the

Department of Education and on the volunteer efforts of a review committee composed of

professionals from institutions of higher education at existing Maine institutions. The Department coordinates the process and delivers the review committee's findings to the State

Boa rd of Education for a final vote. The State has seen an increase in applications for institutional approvals in Maine during the past three years, and a lack of Department capacity

and review committee volunteers has created a potential bottleneck for institutions seeking _

state approval.

LD 2098 may generate a modest savings to the Maine Department of Education, and only in years when a new institution applies for initial applications. The following breakdown of
revenues is an estimate based on other similar sized states and cross referenced with the labor

required for these types of reviews:

i

0 Out of State, with Physical Presence: $1,000

0 In State, New Institution with Physical Presence: $500

0 Out of State, not SARA Participants, no Physical Presence: $250

LD 2098 would also allow the State Boa rd of Education to avoid duplicative institutional reviews in specific circumstances. Under the current Rule Chapter 149, an institution looking to move from temporary, program-based approval in Maine to full degree-granting authorization would
need to undergo a new state review with a new review committee report using exactly the same standards and evidence. LD 2098 would allow the State Board to forego that duplicate review at their own discretion if an institution has already passed a state review in the last five
years.
For these reasons, the Maine Department of Education is in support of L.D. 2098, An Act to
Qpdate Certain Higher Education Statutes. l am happy to answer any questions the Committee may have, and I will be available for work sessions on this bill.

To: Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs From: Heather Albert-Knopp, Chief Operating Officer, College of the Atlantic, halbert-knop_p@coa.edu, 207-801-5603 Re: LD 2098, An Act to Update Certain Higher Education Statutes Date: February 18, 2026
Since its founding more than fifty years ago, College of the Atlantic (COA) has offered a distinctive interdisciplinary, experiential liberal arts education. The college's pedagogy is grounded in the concept of "human ecology," an approach
that examines how we as humans interact with the environments around us --
whether those environments are social, ecological, or built/technological. Under
the umbrella of our one B.A. degree in Human Ecology, COA students study a
range of disciplines from marine science and conservation biology to law, policy, entrepreneurship, and the arts.
ln 1973, when the Maine State Legislature originally authorized College of the Atlantic as a degree-conferring institution (Private and Special Law 1973, Chapter 29), that authorization was limited to granting a Bachelor of Arts degree in Human Ecology. As our institution has grown and evolved over time, we remain committed to human ecology as our pedagogical approach and a central part of our institutional mission, but we now seek to expand our authorization to be able to
confer other degrees at the Bachelor's level.
Specifically, COA has recently been asked to serve as the primary teach--out
partner for Vermont's Sterling College, which will be closing its doors after the
current semester. Sterling offers a sole B.A. degree in Environmental Studies. We
have drafted a teach-out agreement that was accepted by our accreditors at the
New England Commission of Higher Education (NECHE), which would allow COA
to teach-out the B.A. in Environmental Studies for upper-class Sterling College
students. However, in order to do so, we must broaden our authorization to grant additional degrees, beyond Human Ecology, at the Bachelor's level.
It is our understanding that Maine state law regarding degree--granting
authorization has changed since our initial 'l973 authorization, and now institutions
